summary.text: A 78-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus taking sitagliptin was diagnosed with stage IIIC1 (T1b2N1M0) cervical squamous cell carcinoma and treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy, with a complete response. Three years later pelvic MRI showed recurrent tumors in the uterine cervix and vesicouterine pouch, and abdominal CT showed right hydronephrosis. Serum creatinine of 1.30 mg/dL improved to 0.77 mg/dL after right nephrostomy.

Chemotherapy with paclitaxel, carboplatin and pembrolizumab was started for the recurrence, and the next cycle was delayed because of general fatigue. On day 34 after chemotherapy administration she vomited, with blood glucose 539 mg/dL. Urine ketones were strongly positive (3+), arterial pH was 7.159, C-peptide was 0.25 ng/mL and she had Kussmaul respiration. She was diagnosed with DKA due to fulminant T1DM and started on intravenous fluids and continuous Humulin R; anti-GAD antibodies were later negative.

On the following day her condition deteriorated further, with drowsiness (GCS 13) and blood glucose rising to 873 mg/dL. Arterial pH dropped to 7.13, indicating worsening DKA, and mechanical ventilation was initiated. Dark red vomitus and melena indicated upper gastrointestinal bleeding, and hemoglobin fell from 9.9 to 7.7 g/dL. Endoscopy showed extensive mucosal necrosis and contrast-enhanced CT showed contrast defects suggestive of ischemia and necrosis of the stomach and small intestine without thrombus.

Surgical resection was not performed because her general condition was too compromised, and best supportive care was implemented after thorough discussions with her family. She died of septic shock later the same day.
